### Set output to static in astro.config.mjs

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/reference/configuration-reference.mdx

Specify the output target for builds. 'static' prerenders all pages by default; 'server' enables SSR for all pages.

```javascript
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  output: 'static'
});
```

--------------------------------

### Build static Astro site

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/deploy/fleek.mdx

Executes the build command to generate static files in the default `dist/` directory.

```bash
npm run build
```

--------------------------------

### Custom 404 for static assets

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/deploy/cloudflare.mdx

Configures not_found_handling on the Workers static assets to serve a custom 404 page, relevant to the static-asset static site configuration used in deployment.

```jsonc
{
  "assets": {
    "directory": "./dist",
    "not_found_handling": "404-page"
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Static output by default and adapter only needed for on-demand rendering

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/on-demand-rendering.mdx

Explains that Astro pages are pre-rendered at build time as static pages by default, and that a server adapter is only required to render pages on demand (SSR), so a purely static booking landing page needs no adapter.

```mdx
Your Astro project code must be **rendered** to HTML in order to be displayed on the web. 

By default, Astro pages, routes, and API endpoints will be pre-rendered at build time as static pages. However, you can choose to render some or all of your routes on demand by a server when a route is requested.

On-demand rendered pages and routes are generated per visit, and can be customized for each viewer. For example, a page rendered on demand can show a logged-in user their account information or display freshly updated data without requiring a full-site rebuild.

On-demand rendering on the server at request time is also known as **server-side rendering (SSR)**.

## Server adapters

To render any page on demand, you need to add an **adapter**. Each adapter allows Astro to output a script that runs your project on a specific **runtime**: the environment that runs code on the server to generate pages when they are requested (e.g. Netlify, Cloudflare).

You may also wish to add an adapter even if your site is entirely static and you are not rendering any pages on demand.
```

--------------------------------

### Deploy project to Cloudflare with Wrangler

Source: https://github.com/withastro/docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/en/guides/deploy/cloudflare.mdx

Builds the Astro project and deploys the assets to Cloudflare Workers.

```bash
npx astro build && npx wrangler deploy
```
